title: O My Duitara (Ko Duitara Jong Nga)
cultural_context: Celebration of the four-stringed Khasi lute (Duitara) as the voice of the bard's soul, from 'Ki Jingrwai Khasi'.
lyrics_khasi:
Ko duitara jong nga
Ba la thaw na u dieng shnong,
Ki saw tylli ki ksai
Ki pynim la ka dohnud;
Haba nga ktah ia ki,
Ki pynpaw ka sur kynjai,
Ba pynklet ia ki jynjar
Bad pynwan ka jingshai.

Ha kyntoit, ha pynthor,
Mynba iaid marwei,
Me long u paralok
Uba iaineh junom;
Rwai lang bad nga, ko duitara,
Ia ka nam u Hynniewtrep,
Haduh ba ngan da poi
Sha dwar ka jingim ba kut.
lyrics_english:
O my beloved Duitara,
Carved from indigenous village timber,
Your four resonant strings
Bring life unto my spirit;
Whenever my fingers pluck them,
They whisper serenity,
Causing sorrows to fade away
And ushering in the light.

In village lanes, in valley fields,
When journeying alone,
You are the faithful companion
Constant throughout all time;
Sing alongside me, O Duitara,
Praising the glory of the Seven Huts,
Until my earthly steps arrive
At the final threshold of life.

khasi: Ba la thaw na u dieng shnong,
Rwai lang bad nga, ko duitara,
Sha dwar ka jingim ba kut.
english: In village lanes, in valley fields,
Praising the glory of the Seven Huts,
At the final threshold of life.
